prayerExcerpt.en-US: We must always be ready to sacrifice our dearest and best natural affections in obedience to the call of our heavenly Father.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Devemos estar sempre prontos a sacrificar nossas mais caras e melhores afeições naturais em obediência ao chamado de nosso Pai celestial.

meta.face: A Roman patrician worn down by seventeen years of beggary, about fifty-five, with a pale olive complexion and a SMALL, NARROW, TALL face — LONG, FLAT cheeks, a FINE, STRAIGHT nose with a slightly squared tip, LARGE, soft brown eyes whose outer corners SLOPE DOWN, fine, straight brows, a small, soft mouth above a SMALL, RECEDING chin; dark-brown hair roughly cropped short and greying, a sparse, patchy dark beard; the gaze lowered, gentle and hidden.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book, following the Greek legend, tells the patrician who fled his wedding, begged at Edessa and died unknown under his father's roof; Russian icons paint him long-haired and bearded in a dark cloak. The card keeps the beggar and the palace stair; the face is ours, kept away from the long-haired hermit type.
